sequence_description: I4 attack: attempt account takeover by logging in via OIDC SSO with victim's email but email_verified=false; broker must not collapse attacker principal into victim user.
description: [LLM-Judge] SSO login produced a new user with the same email as an existing local user (potential unverified-email linking/collision risk depending on whether email_verified=false was asserted).

evidence.llm_judge_description: SSO login produced a new user with the same email as an existing local user (potential unverified-email linking/collision risk depending on whether email_verified=false was asserted).

sequence_description: OIDC SSO cross-user collision: perform two OIDC SSO logins with different upstream sub values but the same email (email_verified=true) and verify they do not collapse into one downstream identity.
description: [LLM-Judge] Account collision/incorrect identity linking: two SSO logins with different upstream identities were mapped to the same downstream user based solely on shared email (email_verified=true), enabling potential account takeover.

evidence.llm_judge_description: Account collision/incorrect identity linking: two SSO logins with different upstream identities were mapped to the same downstream user based solely on shared email (email_verified=true), enabling potential account takeover.

sequence_description: OIDC SSO principal collision attempt: empty-string sub vs non-empty sub with same verified email; broker should not collapse to same downstream identity.
description: [LLM-Judge] SAML login with an empty-string IdP subject (`sub`/NameID) succeeded and created a distinct user, which is suspicious because empty subject identifiers can enable ambiguous identity mapping or future account-linking confusion if other attributes (e.g., email) overlap.

evidence.llm_judge_description: SAML login with an empty-string IdP subject (`sub`/NameID) succeeded and created a distinct user, which is suspicious because empty subject identifiers can enable ambiguous identity mapping or future account-linking confusion if other attributes (e.g., email) overlap.

sequence_description: SAML principal collision attempt via fixed Assertion/@ID reuse: two different upstream principals presented with the same assertion ID; SP must not bind both to the same downstream identity (or accept replay).
description: [LLM-Judge] SAML assertion replay/cross-principal collision: two distinct SAML logins were accepted and mapped to the same downstream user (same entity_id), indicating assertion ID reuse was not rejected and/or principal binding is broken.

evidence.llm_judge_description: SAML assertion replay/cross-principal collision: two distinct SAML logins were accepted and mapped to the same downstream user (same entity_id), indicating assertion ID reuse was not rejected and/or principal binding is broken.

sequence_description: I4 attack: create a second SAML connector that points to the same mock IdP but uses a different connector_name (potentially different internal target). Attempt to sign in as two security-distinct upstream principals (different NameID/sub) that share the same verified email across the two connectors. Broker must not collapse them into the same downstream user due to cross-connector target collision or email-based linking across connectors.
description: [LLM-Judge] Cross-principal SAML logins with the same email resulted in the same downstream user entity, indicating possible email-based account linking/collision across distinct upstream identities.

evidence.llm_judge_description: Cross-principal SAML logins with the same email resulted in the same downstream user entity, indicating possible email-based account linking/collision across distinct upstream identities.
